title: Music ducking is a fixed -12 dB, chosen by measuring the music UNDER the voice — and that is how to check it
summary: duckMusic lowers the music a fixed 12 dB while the voice speaks (120 ms look-ahead, 450 ms release, pauses under 350 ms held). The design was picked by measurement, not preference: a fixed-depth envelope ducked every word by the same amount (0.1 dB spread across 8 words) while a compressor-style duck followed each syllable (4-5.5 dB spread, audible pumping). You cannot measure music under speech on a real song — they share frequencies — so use an 11 kHz test tone the voice cannot produce and isolate it with a high-pass (not 15 kHz: the AAC encoder removes it). Live proof: -56.2 dB under speech vs -44.0 dB in the pause (12.2 dB), control without duckMusic flat at -44.0 dB. SPI3-70 (2026-09-28): speech is now detected the way Di-Atomic's ducking gate detects it (48 kHz, 10 ms windows above max(peak-40, -55) dBFS, runs under 100 ms dropped) and the duck holds 150 ms after each run before releasing; their gate's pump on a real render went 7.95 -> 0.31 dB (limit 3).
references: SpiderIQ PR #4188 (SC-465, merged 2026-09-22) — the audio lane; ducking design comparison recorded in docs/services/SpiderVideo/LEARNINGS.md 'Ducking was chosen by measuring the music UNDER the voice'
